notes: Rome is walkable. Metro lines A and B are limited; bus 64 goes to the Vatican. The Leonardo Express to Fiumicino costs 14 EUR. The Roma Pass (48 or 72 hours) covers museums and transport.
Timed online tickets are essential for the Colosseum, Vatican Museums and Borghese. Book Borghese weeks ahead and the Vatican 60 days ahead.
Summer reaches 33-38°C: finish the ancient sites by 08:30, spend 13:00-16:00 indoors or in a siesta, and eat dinner after 20:00. Some trattorias close in August for Ferragosto.
Rome's four classic pastas: carbonara, cacio e pepe, amatriciana and gricia. Coperto (cover charge) is 2-3 EUR, and tipping means rounding up.
Cover shoulders and knees in churches (the Vatican is strict). The street fountains (nasoni) give drinkable water, so refill your bottle.
Watch for pickpockets on bus 64 and at Termini. At Trevi and Spagna, say 'no grazie' to bracelet sellers.

stops.name: Colosseo
stops.tips: One ticket covers the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine (about 18 EUR). Book the 08:30 first slot online. The arena floor costs extra, there is no shade, so bring water.

stops.name: Foro Romano
stops.tips: Included in the same ticket. Walk along the Via Sacra to the Temple of Vesta.

stops.name: Palatino
stops.tips: Imperial palaces and views over the Forum, plus an orange garden.

stops.name: Trattoria Luzzi
stops.tips: A cheap, no-frills local trattoria next to the Colosseum. Try the cacio e pepe; the queue moves fast.

stops.name: Piazza del Campidoglio
stops.tips: Michelangelo's square. The terrace behind it has a free sunset view over the Forum.

backups.name: Li Rioni Pizzeria
backups.tips: Roman-style pizza near the Colosseum, open in the evening.

backups.name: Basilica di San Clemente
backups.tips: A three-level church (built over a Roman temple), right next to the Colosseum.

stops.name: Musei Vaticani
stops.tips: Book the 08:00 first slot for the Sistine Chapel (25 EUR online, 60 days ahead). Expect the Raphael Rooms and long corridors.

stops.name: Basilica di San Pietro
stops.tips: Free, but there is a security queue. The dome costs 10 EUR (551 steps), and the Pietà is by the entrance.

stops.name: Bonci Pizzarium
stops.tips: Gabriele Bonci's pizza by the slice, eaten standing up. Nearest metro: Cipro (Vatican).

stops.name: Castel Sant'Angelo
stops.tips: Hadrian's mausoleum turned fortress, with a terrace view of the Vatican.

stops.name: Ponte Sant'Angelo
stops.tips: Bernini's bridge lined with angels. Take your photos before sunset.

backups.name: Pizzeria Da Remo Testaccio
backups.tips: Thin Roman pizza in Testaccio, open in the evening.

backups.name: Giardini Vaticani
backups.tips: Guided tour of the Vatican Gardens, as an alternative to the castle.

days.theme: Baroque Rome: Pantheon, Navona and Trevi

stops.name: Pantheon
stops.tips: See the oculus in the dome. Entry is 5 EUR; morning light is best, and there is Mass on Sundays.

stops.name: Piazza Navona
stops.tips: Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers. The cafés are pricey, so come for the photos.

stops.name: Campo de' Fiori
stops.tips: Morning market with cheese, spices and truffle products.

stops.name: Roscioli Salumeria
stops.tips: Carbonara and a deli counter, among the best in Rome. Booking is essential.

stops.name: Trevi Fountain
stops.tips: Toss in a coin. It is empty at 07:00 or 23:00 and packed by day (entry system in place since 2025).

backups.name: Armando al Pantheon
backups.tips: Roman cooking since 1961, next to the Pantheon. Reserve ahead.

backups.name: Galleria Doria Pamphilj
backups.tips: A private palace collection with Caravaggio and Velázquez, a calmer option than Trevi.

stops.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
stops.tips: One of Rome's oldest churches dedicated to Mary, with golden mosaics. Quiet in the morning.

stops.name: Trastevere Streets
stops.tips: Cobblestones and ivy-covered walls; head along Via della Lungaretta.

stops.name: Da Enzo al 29
stops.tips: A small Trastevere classic serving amatriciana and artichokes. Join the queue when it opens at 12:00.

stops.name: Villa Farnesina
stops.tips: A Renaissance villa with Raphael frescoes. Peaceful.

stops.name: Gianicolo Terrace
stops.tips: Rome's best free view, with the Garibaldi monument. Come at sunset.

backups.name: Trapizzino Trastevere
backups.tips: Stew stuffed into a pizza pocket. Street food.

backups.name: Orto Botanico di Roma
backups.tips: A botanical garden in Trastevere, as an alternative to the villa.

stops.name: Galleria Borghese
stops.tips: Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in a 2-hour slot. Booking weeks ahead is mandatory.

stops.name: Villa Borghese Gardens
stops.tips: A park walk; from the Pincio terrace you look over Piazza del Popolo.

stops.name: Spanish Steps
stops.tips: No sitting on the steps. Via Condotti is nearby.

stops.name: Pastificio Guerra
stops.tips: Fresh pasta for 5 EUR behind the Spanish Steps. There is a queue at 13:00.

stops.name: Ara Pacis
stops.tips: Augustus's altar of peace, housed in Richard Meier's glass pavilion. Air-conditioned.

backups.name: Ginger Sapori e Salute
backups.tips: A light Italian lunch near Spagna.

backups.name: Piazza del Popolo
backups.tips: Twin churches and a Caravaggio (Santa Maria del Popolo, free).

stops.name: Ostia Antica
stops.tips: 30 minutes from Rome (metro and train). A port city as well preserved as Pompeii, with mosaic-floored baths. There is little shade.

stops.name: Ostia Lido Beach
stops.tips: 10 minutes from the ancient city, this is the Romans' own beach. A stabilimento (private beach club) sunbed costs 10-20 EUR.

stops.name: Ristorante Ostia Lido Balık
stops.tips: Seafood on the beach, best between lunch and dinner.

backups.name: Sbarco di Enea Ostia
backups.tips: A trattoria by the Ostia Antica exit.

backups.name: Frascati
backups.tips: A wine town in the hills outside Rome, as an alternative to Ostia.

stops.name: Mercato Testaccio
stops.tips: A local market. At Mordi e Vai, try the beef stew sandwich and supplì (fried rice balls).

stops.name: Pyramid of Cestius and Non-Catholic Cemetery
stops.tips: A pyramid in Rome and the Keats-Shelley cemetery, with resident cats.

stops.name: Aventine Orange Garden
stops.tips: Giardino degli Aranci and the Knights of Malta keyhole: a farewell view.

stops.name: Flavio al Velavevodetto
stops.tips: A trattoria carved into Monte Testaccio. Order the carbonara and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew).

stops.name: Roma Termini
stops.tips: The Leonardo Express reaches Fiumicino in 32 minutes. Time to say goodbye.

backups.name: Trapizzino Testaccio
backups.tips: Stew in a pizza pocket, a quick farewell bite.

backups.name: Baths of Caracalla
backups.tips: The vast ruins of a Roman bathhouse, as an alternative to the pyramid.
